headline: Kenya Shilling Slips to 130 Per Dollar Amid Importer Demand
summary: The Kenyan shilling weakened slightly to trade around 130.20 per US dollar, pressured by increased greenback demand from commercial importers ahead of the central bank's upcoming rate decision.
why: Exchange rate fluctuations in frontier African economies impact import costs and domestic consumer price inflation.

impacts.name: Kenyan Shilling
impacts.why: Strong importer demand for foreign currency drives down the local currency exchange value.
